title: Idempotent offsets, resumable streams, and backfill strategy for SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Product requirements for a consistent, resumable streaming and pagination contract across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Defines idempotent offset semantics, client resume protocols, backfill strategy when tokens expire, and explicit compatibility constraints for older clients.
background: Customers building real-time and fanout features have reported fragile resumptions after transient network failures and difficulty reconciling partial reads across SDKs. Existing cursor-only semantics lead to ambiguous ordering for high-throughput fanout and complicate deterministic backfills. This PRD defines a unified approach (idempotent offsets + opaque resume tokens + explicit backfill path) to make resume behavior predictable and testable across SDK languages.
goals: Define a single resume token model that is language-agnostic and supports deterministic backfill
Provide clear SDK ergonomics for Python (async generator), TypeScript (AsyncIterable), and Go (channel/iterator) to resume streams with minimal boilerplate
Specify retry semantics that differentiate idempotent fetches vs side-effecting operations and are configurable by client teams
Ensure backward compatibility with cursor-v1 while allowing server-side rollout of cursor-v2 (offset-aware)
non_goals: Significant server-side state retention beyond the configurable retention window (we will not guarantee infinite replay)
Rewriting existing long-running non-idempotent RPCs into idempotent ones (those require separate product work)
Full wire-level protocol migration for older SDKs — we will support graceful degradation instead
requirements: Server: introduce 'resume_token_v2' that encodes: last_sequence_number, partition_id (when applicable), and server_retention_epoch. Token must be opaque to clients.
Server: maintain replay buffer for retention_window (default 72h) and return explicit 'token_expired' error when a resume token points to data outside retention window.
Clients: treat pagination cursors as opaque. When server offers resume_token_v2, SDK should prefer it for streaming endpoints to allow offset-accurate resumes.
Pagination: support both opaque cursor pagination (next_cursor) for generic use and offset-based pages (limit, offset_hint) for deterministic ordering and cross-client reconciliation.
Retries: default retry policy for idempotent list/fetch/stream-continued requests: exponential backoff with full jitter; base_delay=200ms, max_delay=8s, max_attempts=5. Allow overrides per-client.
Retries: non-idempotent endpoints (create/update) must not be automatically retried by default; SDK offers opt-in idempotency via client-provided idempotency_key where server supports it.

Streaming resume: client must send last_ack_seq when reconnecting. Server will return items with seq > last_ack_seq; if last_ack_seq < earliest_seq_in_retention, server returns token_expired and provides earliest_seq and suggested start token.
Heartbeat/keepalive: streaming protocol includes heartbeat frames. SDKs must expose hooks for heartbeat events so applications can monitor liveness.

Backfill: server exposes a 'backfill' API for historical gaps beyond streaming retention; backfill is asynchronous and may require a job token. SDKs expose a helper that polls backfill job and streams completed records into the same resumable interface.

Language ergonomics: a) Python: AsyncResumableIterator with resume(token) and checkpoint() methods. b) TypeScript: AsyncIterable & controller.resume(token) returning an AsyncIterable. c) Go: ResumableIterator interface with Resume(token) error and Next() (item, err).
Compatibility: server must respond with client-compatible cursor version in headers (X-Cursor-Version). SDKs must fall back to cursor-v1 behavior when v2 is unavailable and surface a console warning.
Testing: include interop tests that validate resume across languages: simulate disconnects, expired tokens, and backfill flows. Provide recorded fixtures used by CI.
acceptance_criteria: Python SDK exposes AsyncResumableIterator; sample app can disconnect and resume from token within retention window and observe no duplicate processing of items (idempotency tested via sequence numbers)
TypeScript SDK exposes resume() helper that returns an AsyncIterable which resumes at the correct sequence when provided resume_token_v2
Go SDK provides Resume(token) and passes integration test where simulated network failures are triggered and client fetches remaining items without loss or duplication
Server returns token_expired with earliest_seq and suggested_start_token when resume token points before retention window; SDK surfaces a clear exception and a helper to trigger backfill
Retry policy exercised in CI: idempotent fetch attempts succeed within configured retry limits; non-idempotent calls are not retried by default and are clearly documented
Interop tests included in PR: at least one end-to-end test per language in the monorepo CI, and a documented manual smoke test guide in Confluence
Migration doc in repo (docs/sdk/resume-migration.md) linked from PR, with code snippets for both old cursor usage and new resume_token_v2 usage
api_examples:
# Python example
async for item in client.events.stream(resume_token=token):
  process(item)
# get checkpoint
new_token = await client.events.checkpoint()

// Server response example (HTTP header): X-Cursor-Version: v2
// Error body when expired: {"error":"token_expired", "earliest_seq": 12345, "suggested_start": "<new_token>" }
implementation_notes: Rollout strategy: stage 1 - server emits resume_token_v2 on experimental routes behind feature flag; SDKs add opt-in support. Stage 2 - enable by default for new streaming endpoints; Stage 3 - announce deprecation window for old cursor-only semantics.
Compatibility: keep cursors opaque; do not require SDKs to parse token internals. Only server components understand sequence math; clients send back tokens or last_ack_seq numbers.

Backfill UX: SDK helper will abstract backfill job polling and will merge backfill results into the client's resume stream with a flag 'from_backfill' on items so apps can treat them differently if needed.
Telemetry: SDKs must emit metrics for: resume_attempts, resume_success, token_expired_events, backfill_jobs_started, and resume_duplicate_detected. Map to console dashboards for rollout monitoring.
Docs: create migration guide, quickstart snippets for 3 languages, and troubleshooting checklist (token_expired, missing_partitions, out_of_order).
Perf: ensure streaming resume path maintains ordering guarantees for single partition streams. Multi-partition fanout may provide eventual ordering guarantees; document explicitly.
migration_plan: Publish SDK alpha with resume_token_v2 support behind feature flag; run canary apps (internal infra) to validate behavior
Add interop tests and run cross-language CI matrices (Python/TS/Go) against a test server with intentional disconnect injections
Update docs and notify customers via release notes explaining new semantics, retention window, and backfill options
After 6 weeks of canary stability, flip feature flag for new streaming endpoints and add deprecation note for cursor-v1 in console and API docs
risks: Retention window too small -> frequent token_expired events and poor UX. Mitigation: set conservative default and provide clear console metric for token_expired rate.
Clients incorrectly deduplicate items leading to data loss. Mitigation: include sequence numbers on items and test dedupe helpers in SDKs.
Backfill overload on server if many clients request large historical ranges. Mitigation: rate-limit backfill jobs and queue heavy backfills as offline jobs with quotas.
qa_plan: Unit tests for SDK helpers (resume, checkpoint, backfill helper) in each language
Integration tests: simulated disconnects, token_expired flows, backfill completion in CI
E2E interop: orchestrated test across Python/TS/Go clients to validate identical ordering for single-partition stream
Performance test: resume latency under 100ms median for recent tokens within retention window
Chaos test: inject intermittent network failures and verify no duplicates or gaps when resume is used
notes: 10mar: initial draft captured during cross-functional sync. Key ask: unify resume semantics to reduce client-side complexity.
11mar: runtime leads flagged retention window as tunable knob; agreed default 72h and expose project-level override.
12mar: design review: prefer opaque tokens to avoid client parsing; SDKs will not decode internals. Action: engineering to produce token schema doc.
Followups: add sample app in 'examples/resumable-streams' repo and schedule API review with platform security for token lifecycle.
